case_name: Vishvas Aba Kurane v State of Maharashtra
respondent:
State of Maharashtra
Supreme Court of India

19 January 1978
C.As. Nos. 166 of 1971 and 201 of 1973.
The Judgment was delivered by: JASWANT SINGH, J.
1.   Vishvas Aba Kurane, appellant in Criminal Appeal 166 of 1971 and Akaram Bhairu Kotwal, appellant in Criminal Appeal 201 of 1973 (hereinafter referred to for the sake of brevity as 'Vishvas' and 'Akaram' respectively) who were charged and tried along with three brothers of the latter viz. facts: On May 17, 1968, a scuffle broke out between Akaram and Abdul Ghani at a local cinema.
Jaywant intervened on behalf of Abdul Ghani, and the two groups set upon each other with 'chappals'.
The combatants took their seats as the show started, but the tussle was renewed during the interval.
On May 18, 1968, another fracas broke out between Maruti and Dinkar, which did not assume a grave turn.
On May 19, 1968, Jaywant left his house to keep a vigil and went to Babu Ranadive's shop for a 'panpatti'.
Mahadev and Ibrahim appeared armed with sticks and mauled Jaywant, who managed to extricate himself and run towards the well.
Jaywant cried out that he had been beaten, and after raising an alarm, he turned back and asked Mahadev and Ibrahim why they had manhandled him.
Ibrahim tried to assault Jaywant with a stick, but before he could do so, Jaywant lifted him bodily and threw him on the ground.
Ramchandra Gayakwad rushed to the scene and wrested the stick from Ibrahim.
Vishvas arrived armed with an axe and accompanied by Akaram, Shiva, and Maruti, who were armed with sticks.
The accused administered an axe blow on Jaywant's shoulder, and he became unconscious and slumped in front of the Central Bank building.
Raghunath and Shankar rushed to the scene, saw Jaywant lying on the ground, and turned back when they saw the accused approaching them.
Akaram caught hold of Raghunath while Vishvas and Mahadev whipped out knives and inflicted injuries on his forehead, back, and right thigh.
Vishvas and Shiva also caused injuries on Shankar's person with a knife and stick respectively.
A scuffle ensued between Raghunath and Shankar on one side and the accused on the other, in which Shankar picked up a stick and used it against some of the accused.
Ananda, a cousin of Raghunath, was also assaulted by some of the accused.
The accused decamped after being told that they had achieved their object.
Raghunath succumbed to his injuries at 9:45 p.m. while being examined and treated by the Medical Officer.
issues: Whether the accused intentionally caused the death of Raghunath Sidu Nikam
Whether the accused formed an unlawful assembly and pursued their fleeing victims with the object of assaulting them
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution argued that the accused intentionally caused the death of Raghunath Sidu Nikam
The prosecution argued that the accused formed an unlawful assembly and pursued their fleeing victims with the object of assaulting them
respondent_arguments: The defense argued that the accused did not form an unlawful assembly until after the first assault on Jaywant
The defense argued that the accused had a right to self-defense after Jaywant bodily lifted Ibrahim and threw him on the ground
court_reasoning: The trial Court found that Raghunath died as a result of the injuries inflicted on him
The trial Court held that the accused formed an unlawful assembly and pursued their fleeing victims with the object of assaulting them
The trial Court held that the accused exceeded the right of private defense which they had earlier acquired as against Jaywant
holding: The High Court convicted the appellants for the murder of Raghunath Sidu Nikam and sentenced them to imprisonment for life
The sentences imposed on Vishvas, appellant, and Mahadev were ordered to run concurrently
